subject: Day 1: Your first three thank-yous
title: Begin with what's already in front of you.
body:
Good morning.

You don't need a perfect month to begin a gratitude practice. You just need a few quiet minutes and a willingness to notice.

Read today's psalm slowly. Then start a list you can return to every day—on paper, in a journal, or on your phone.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: One person, one everyday provision, and one small joy.

subject: Day 2: Don't let the good go unnoticed
title: Today, gratitude begins with remembering.
body:
Good morning.

Some gifts become so familiar that we stop noticing them. Today's psalm invites us to remember God's goodness.

Think about what has sustained you lately. Include the ordinary things; they belong on this list, too.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Three ways you've been cared for recently.

subject: Day 3: Step outside and notice
title: Let creation give you a place to begin.
body:
Good morning.

The sky doesn't need words to point us toward God. Neither does the morning light falling across your kitchen table.

Take a moment to look beyond your to-do list. What beauty has been waiting for your attention?

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Three things in creation that made you pause.

subject: Day 4: Thankful for enough
title: Notice what has carried you through today.
body:
Good morning.

Green pastures and dark valleys appear in the same psalm. Gratitude can make room for both comfort and difficulty.

You don't have to pretend everything is easy. Start with the care you can recognize right where you are.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something that nourishes you, something that restores you, and someone who walks beside you.

subject: Day 5: The kindness you still remember
title: Some gifts stay with us for years.
body:
Good morning.

This psalm gathers stories of trouble, help, and thanksgiving. Your list can hold stories, too.

Remember a time when help arrived through a person, an opportunity, or an unexpected kindness.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Three moments of help you don't want to forget.

subject: Day 6: A little wonder goes a long way
title: You don't have to look far to find something remarkable.
body:
Good morning.

A vast sky. A tiny hand. The surprising detail of a leaf.

Today's psalm holds wonder at creation alongside wonder that God cares for people. Let yourself slow down enough to be amazed.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something vast, something small, and something wonderfully ordinary.

subject: Day 7: One week, 21 reasons
title: Take a moment to see what you've collected.
body:
Good morning.

You've reached the end of your first week. If you've missed a day, simply begin again here.

Read through your list before adding today's entries. Which memory brings back a smile?

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A gift from this morning, a gift from this week, and a gift you're still enjoying.

subject: Day 8: Goodness you can taste
title: Today's gratitude might begin at your table.
body:
Good morning.

Some reminders of goodness are wonderfully tangible: warm bread, cool water, a familiar meal, a seat beside someone you love.

Let an ordinary moment become an invitation to give thanks.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something you've tasted, something you've enjoyed, and something you've shared.

subject: Day 9: You weren't meant to do life alone
title: Remember the people who help you belong.
body:
Good morning.

Today's invitation to worship is shared: come, sing, bow down. There is something precious about turning toward God together.

Think about the people who make room for you, encourage your faith, or help you feel at home.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Three people or communities you're grateful for—and why.

subject: Day 10: Mercy worth remembering
title: Give thanks for the chance to begin again.
body:
Good morning.

The repeated refrain of this psalm keeps bringing us back to God's enduring love.

Our memories sometimes need that repetition. Today, remember the kindness that has met you more than once.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A fresh start, a patient person, and a mercy you've received.

subject: Day 11: Look at what helped you grow
title: There's a story behind what sustains you.
body:
Good morning.

A harvest depends on much we cannot rush: rain, preparation, tending, and time.

Think about the good things in your life that grew gradually. Who helped nurture them?

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something that grew, someone who tended it, and a provision you received along the way.

subject: Day 12: A thank-you with someone's name on it
title: Gratitude gets richer when it gets specific.
body:
Good morning.

This psalm celebrates God's goodness and the telling of it from one generation to another.

Whose words or example helped you recognize that goodness? Remember the people who gave you something worth carrying forward.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Three things someone has taught you through their kindness, faith, or example.

subject: Day 13: When gratitude includes relief
title: Remember a burden that became lighter.
body:
Good morning.

Today's psalm remembers distress and gives thanks for help. Some of our deepest gratitude comes with a long exhale.

You may still be waiting for relief in one part of life. You can honor that while remembering help elsewhere.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A burden eased, a comfort received, and a moment of joy.

subject: Day 14: Make room for a little joy
title: Your list has room for delight.
body:
Good morning.

This psalm overflows with music and celebration. Today, let your gratitude include things that simply make you glad.

A favorite song counts. So does a ridiculous joke or a happy memory that catches you by surprise.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something that makes you sing, something that makes you laugh, and something worth celebrating.

subject: Day 15: Halfway—and already a keepsake
title: Look back before you write today's three.
body:
Good morning.

You're halfway through the challenge. Your growing list is becoming a record of what you've noticed and remembered.

Read a few earlier entries. What might you have forgotten if you hadn't written it down?

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Three gifts from this month you want your future self to remember.

subject: Day 16: Thankful someone listened
title: Being heard is a gift.
body:
Good morning.

The psalmist gives thanks for being heard in distress. Today, consider the comfort of bringing your honest voice to God.

Remember, too, the people who have listened without rushing you or trying to fix everything.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Someone who listened, a prayer you could speak honestly, and a comfort you received.

subject: Day 17: Small psalm, meaningful pause
title: Two verses can give you plenty to carry today.
body:
Good morning.

Today's reading is short enough to read twice. Let its words about God's love and faithfulness settle in.

Your gratitude entries can be simple, too. They don't need to impress anyone; they just need to be yours.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Three small things that made today better.

subject: Day 18: This day has something to notice
title: Start with the day you actually have.
body:
Good morning.

Some days invite celebration. Others ask for endurance.

As you read, look for a reason to thank God within the reality of today. A small kindness is worth recording even when the day is complicated.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something helpful, something hopeful, and something good about today.

subject: Day 19: Where has help come from?
title: Remember what supported your next step.
body:
Good morning.

This psalm turns our attention toward God's keeping care.

Think about the support you've received along your own road: guidance, practical help, companionship, or strength for the next step.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Help you received, guidance you were given, and someone who showed up.

subject: Day 20: Remember when joy returned
title: Some memories deserve to be written down.
body:
Good morning.

Tears and joy both have a place in this psalm. You can bring your whole story to today's reading.

Remember a moment when laughter returned, hope stirred, or something good surprised you after a difficult season.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A happy memory, a sign of hope, and a person who shared your joy.

subject: Day 21: The gift of being together
title: Notice the relationships that bring peace.
body:
Good morning.

Being together can be a gift, especially when there is kindness, patience, and room to be yourself.

Today, notice the people who make connection feel possible—in your family, neighborhood, church, or circle of friends.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A welcoming place, a peaceful interaction, and a relationship you treasure.

subject: Day 22: Thanks for the strength to keep going
title: Remember what helped you take another step.
body:
Good morning.

Today's psalm includes thanksgiving for strength in response to prayer.

Think about a day when you kept going with help you didn't manufacture alone. What steadied you?

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: An encouraging word, practical support, and strength for something difficult.

subject: Day 23: Known, seen, and wonderfully made
title: Give thanks for the details that make a person unique.
body:
Good morning.

This psalm reflects on being deeply known by God. Let that invitation lead you toward care for the person you are.

Consider the abilities, experiences, and distinctive qualities you can offer others.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: An ability you value, a part of your story that shaped you, and a quality you appreciate in someone else.

subject: Day 24: Care that reaches the vulnerable
title: Notice goodness expressed through action.
body:
Good morning.

Today's psalm praises God's care for people who need help, food, freedom, and welcome.

Look for the people who put compassion into practice around you. Their work may be quiet, but it matters.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Someone who serves, a kindness you witnessed, and care you've received.

subject: Day 25: There's room for a tender heart
title: Gratitude doesn't require you to feel cheerful.
body:
Good morning.

The God praised in this psalm also attends to the brokenhearted.

If this season feels tender, let your list be gentle. Record what offers comfort without asking it to erase what hurts.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A source of comfort, a safe person, and a small moment of peace.

subject: Day 26: Let everything join the thank-you
title: Look beyond your usual list.
body:
Good morning.

This psalm invites all creation into praise—from the heavens to the smallest creatures.

Let it widen your attention. What have you walked past, relied upon, or enjoyed without really noticing?

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something outdoors, something easily overlooked, and something that fills you with wonder.

subject: Day 27: Your gratitude has a story
title: Choose one thank-you you could share at the table.
body:
Good morning.

The psalmist invites others to hear what God has done. Your list holds stories someone else might love to hear.

Choose one entry and add a sentence about why it matters. Save it to share over a meal or in a conversation.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Three meaningful moments with a little story behind each.

subject: Day 28: The ordinary things keeping us going
title: Today, notice the gifts that sustain daily life.
body:
Good morning.

Today's psalm pays attention to a world full of life, provision, and rhythms of work and rest.

Consider how much supports an ordinary day. Let your thank-yous become specific.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something that feeds you, something that helps you work, and something that helps you rest.

subject: Day 29: Who helped you learn gratitude?
title: Remember the goodness passed down to you.
body:
Good morning.

Remembering and telling are woven through this psalm. Gratitude can be something we receive from others and pass along.

Think of a story, tradition, or example that taught you to notice goodness.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A meaningful tradition, a story worth keeping, and a person whose example stays with you.

subject: Day 30: Ninety reasons worth keeping
title: Finish your list—and make a place for it.
body:
Good morning.

Today's psalm closes the book with praise. Today, you close this challenge with a record of the gifts you've noticed.

If you wrote three things each day, you now have 90. If your list is shorter, it still holds something worth keeping.

Date your list and save it. Read a few favorites aloud with someone you love.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A gift from this month, something this practice helped you notice, and a blessing you want to carry forward.
